$comment: Where `derm connect <agent> --gate` registers derm's gate, one object per agent (wave 4 lane Q, T2.8). Transcribed from the packages that own each gate: lane L's packages/derm-hooks-claude-compat/src/registration.ts (branch wip/L-hooks-claude at 12d2c86), lane N's packages/derm-hooks-native/registration/<agent>/ and its README table (lane/N-hooks-native at 85592cf), and docs/install/agents.md (main at 824ae83) for the agents whose gate installs through their own command. Lane Q keeps this table in its own folder so lanes L, N and P never share a file with it; integration w4 may move each object into its agent's preset row. Placeholders: {command} is the agent's `command` with {node} and {hook_file} filled; {hook_dir} is the package folder given with --hook; {hook_url} is file:// plus that folder; {version} is derm's own version. A string is a placeholder only when it is the whole value, except in `command` and `commands`. `marker` finds derm's own entry, so a second --gate replaces it and never adds a second gate. Step kinds: json-array-entry, json-member, toml-array-entry, toml-set, owned-file, plugin-folder, json-permission (OpenCode's and Kilo's `permission` keys, set only where that narrows), commands (print only). `mergeChain` lists the global files an agent deep-merges, in its order: derm writes the last one that exists (else `path`) and reads the others first. Wave 5b lane 5bF: a command-hook row's `command` is `{derm} hook <agent> <event>`, {derm} being this derm's own real path, a plain path to a file only you or root can write in a folder of the same kind, so no --hook folder and no node (contracts/hook-dialects.md 9.1; rules case 227). `markers` lists what finds derm's own entry: the first is in what derm writes now, the rest in what an older derm wrote, so a second --gate replaces a wave 4 node entry. Step kind text-file writes one file of plain text derm owns alone (Hermes's derm-path), only into a folder that already exists when `folderMustExist`.

agents.source: packages/derm-opencode-plugin/opencode.fragment.json and crates/derm-cli/src/watch/register.rs at 824ae83 (OpenCode 1.19.4 plugin/shared.ts:171-189); the files OpenCode 1.19.4 merges and how, config/config.ts:42-44, 140-148, 272-274, 567-578, permission/index.ts:28-32, util/wildcard.ts:3-19 (lane Q, third chat)
notes: derm writes the last of config.json, opencode.json and opencode.jsonc that exists: OpenCode merges them in that order and a later `plugin` list replaces an earlier one.

The `permission` keys keep OpenCode's own prompts as a second layer. They only narrow: an allow becomes ask, a key is added only beside allows and asks, and a deny, a pattern list or a `tools` switch set to false is left as it is.
A project's own opencode.json, OPENCODE_PERMISSION, OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR's files and an agent's own `permission` are read after these files and can override them; derm does not see them.

agents.name: Kilo Code
agents.source: packages/derm-kilo-plugin/kilo.fragment.json at 824ae83; Kilo 7.8.18 (b817615) config/config.ts:72-75, 460-482, 1024-1034, core/src/global.ts:24, permission/index.ts:106, util/wildcard.ts:3-19 (lane Q, third chat)
notes: derm writes the last of config.json, kilo.json, kilo.jsonc, opencode.json and opencode.jsonc that exists in ~/.config/kilo: Kilo merges them in that order and a later `plugin` list replaces an earlier one. KILO_CONFIG_DIR does not move these files; its own files are read later, like a project's.
The `permission` keys only narrow, as OpenCode's: an allow becomes ask, a key is added only beside allows and asks, and a deny, a pattern list or a `tools` switch set to false is left as it is.
A project's own kilo.json or opencode.json, KILO_PERMISSION, KILO_CONFIG_DIR's files and an agent's own `permission` are read after these files and can override them; derm does not see them.
